findings: FinderService compares MD5 hashes without final byte confirmation. JPEGs are transformed through JpegPatcher before hashing; that implementation remains unread, so this is not established as encoded-byte equality.
Empty files are always skipped even when minLength is zero. DateModifiedTo removes files older than the upper bound, using < instead of >; source-only finding.

Date constraints restrict sourceFiles but not targetFiles, so outside-range files can still appear as matching targets. Whether this is intended anchor-filter semantics requires UI/documentation review.

Directory recursion has no physical-identity visited set or depth/entry limit in this source. Hidden/system directory filtering returns before descendants but each immediate directory was already added by its parent, so its own files can still be scanned.

Case-insensitive excluded-directory comparisons contrast with case-sensitive DistinctBy directory deduplication. No inode/hardlink alias separation is visible in FinderService; DuplicateFile implementation remains unread.

Cancellation throws during enumeration but breaks matching loops and returns a partial FinderResult with no cancelled field. Hashing is synchronous without cancellation checkpoints or a stream disposal finally.

DeleteFilesAsync uses path existence and MoveToRecycleBin without revalidating discovered content or physical identity. A missing path is still counted as actioned. No deletion or recycle-bin operation executed.
adoption: No upstream code adopted. Own exact-file regression suite separately passed 36/36 and already distinguishes physical aliases from byte-confirmed copies.
